title: The MacBook Pro Max Just Dropped to Its Lowest Price Ever
gist: Amazon is selling the 16-inch M5 Max MacBook Pro (36GB RAM, 2TB) for $3,499, 20% off its $4,399 list and $150 below its previous all-time low. The cut comes a week before Apple's rumored announcement of a touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro, which is also expected to use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and after a June price increase across the lineup.

themes.theme: Pre-launch discounting of the M5 Max MacBook Pro

insights.claim: Amazon is selling the 16-inch M5 Max MacBook Pro with 36GB RAM and 2TB storage for $3,499, 20% below its $4,399 list price. That is $400 less than a few days earlier and $150 below the configuration's previous all-time low.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Deep retailer discounts on the outgoing model point to channel inventory clearing ahead of a product transition.

insights.claim: Apple raised prices across the whole MacBook Pro lineup in June 2026, so the current discount stands out more.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: A mid-cycle price increase followed by heavy discounting suggests Apple has pricing power at list but weaker sell-through demand.

insights.claim: Apple is rumored to announce a touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro within a week, which the author calls potentially the biggest change to the lineup in many years. Rumors say it will keep the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chip options.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: The catalyst is a form-factor change (OLED, touch), not a new chip, which matters for Apple's Mac upgrade-cycle story and its OLED panel suppliers.
insights.locator: An exciting new MacBook is rumored

insights.claim: The author says the M5 Max delivers GPU performance never before seen on a MacBook, a big step up from the M4 Max and M5 Pro. In his testing, Cyberpunk 2077 averaged over 60 fps on the Ultra preset without upscaling.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Apple silicon's GPU gains support its push into pro creative work and gaming.

insights.claim: Serious on-device AI work calls for the 64GB or 128GB configurations, which Apple sells only directly and at 'exorbitant' prices; third-party retailers such as Amazon do not stock them.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: High-memory configurations for local AI are a high-margin, direct-channel product for Apple.
insights.locator: If you really want to get serious about AI performance
